answer.rationale: Rollback (memory_b1) is the strongest precedent but is foreclosed by the compliance ruling on the security patch, so it is not actionable regardless of how well it worked on day 18. Regional failover (memory_b2) recovered latency in March, but that record concerns a latency/error degradation, not a write-heavy settlement peak; shifting regions mid-peak risks exactly the in-flight write loss the primary objective forbids. Circuit breaking (memory_b4) contained an external partner failure; nothing here indicates a failing downstream dependency, and failing fast on the write path would drop customer writes. Add capacity (memory_b3) is plausible but that memory describes headroom provisioned in advance of a known peak, not capacity added 90 minutes into an active degradation; provisioning latency likely exceeds the window. That leaves route_read_replicas: memory_b5 is the only inherited record where the observed outcome is specifically write-latency recovery via contention relief on the primary, it is non-destructive, and it loses no writes. I spend the single verification on memory_b5 rather than the blocked rollback, because my whole plan rests on it and the consolidated summary hides the causal detail I need: whether read offload actually caused the write-latency recovery or merely coincided with it, whether the load profile involved heavy concurrent writes as here, and how long relief took to appear. If the source shows the day-55 win came from a lightly-loaded primary or a slow-burn recovery, read routing will not move a 5x p99 inside this window and add_capacity becomes the better call. I therefore commit only to a small guarded test: shift a bounded slice of reporting/read traffic off the primary and watch write p99 and queue depth for a defined interval before extending. Downstream risk to flag: replica-served reads may return stale data, which in a payments context can propagate into reconciliation, settlement reports, and any automated decisioning that consumes them, so read consumers must be marked as potentially stale for the duration. Residual uncertainty is real: I have not established that read contention is the actual cause of the climbing write latency; the release two hours ago remains a live suspect, and since it cannot be reverted, mitigation rather than diagnosis is the near-term aim.
